1	# S16 — Clean Separation: Persona Mode Switcher + De-duplication + P1 Fix
2	
3	## Context
4	
5	S13-S15 consolidated the sidebar (31→13 items), redesigned Settings, and shipped the multi-studio switcher. Production review by the user and Sage surfaced two lingering structural problems:
6	
7	1. **Duplication.** Three destinations still live in two places each — Settings keeps a link *and* the main sidebar keeps a link (or redirect). Feels incoherent, breaks the Stripe/Linear mental model.
8	2. **"All in one SaaS" soup.** Owner sees 13 top-level items covering daily ops, weekly management, and configuration in one flat list. Even grouped, cognitive load stays high. No mental boundary between "my daily work" / "running the business" / "configuring the software."
9	
10	Two asks from the user:
11	- Separate properly (fix the duplication + split by mental mode).
12	- Evaluate an "agency / team account" concept for running multiple studios.
13	
14	Goal: make InkOS feel like **three focused apps in one shell** — Operate / Manage / Configure — with workspace (studio) switching on top. Match the Stripe pattern (Test vs Live modes + workspace picker) rather than a flat everything-sidebar.
15	
16	---
17	
18	## Decisions (locked)
19	
20	### 1. Persona Mode Switcher (primary fix)
21	
22	Sidebar top gets a 3-way segmented control or dropdown: **Operate · Manage · Configure**. Each mode has a distinct sidebar subset.
23	
24	| Mode | Items | Who defaults here |
25	|---|---|---|
26	| **Operate** (daily) | Dashboard · Calendar · Appointments · Clients · Inventory | guest_artist, artist, receptionist |
27	| **Manage** (weekly) | Team · Payments · Commissions · Payroll · Reports · Campaigns · Referrals | admin, owner |
28	| **Configure** (setup) | Settings (full hub) | — (accessed on demand) |
29	
30	Density per screen: 5 / 7 / 1 items (vs today's 13 for owner).
31	
32	**Access rules:**
33	- artist + guest_artist see Operate only (switcher hidden)
34	- receptionist sees Operate + limited Manage (Payments, Reports only — already role-gated)
35	- admin + owner see all three; switcher visible
36	- Active mode persisted in `inkos_active_mode` cookie (mirrors S15's `inkos_active_studio` pattern)
37	- Default by role on first login; user override persists
38	
39	### 2. De-duplication (tactical cleanup)
40	
41	Resolve the three confirmed duplications:
42	
43	| Feature | Keep at | Remove from | Rationale |
44	|---|---|---|---|
45	| **Booking Page** | `Settings > Studio > Booking page` | Remove from APP_NAV `Schedule` group | It's configuration, not a daily task |
46	| **Ink Registry** | `Inventory` tab (already reachable via `/inventory?tab=ink-registry`) | Remove from `SettingsSidebar` Studio group | It's operational (stock-adjacent), not config |
47	| **Roles & Permissions** | `Artists > Permissions` tab (S13 decision) | Remove from `SettingsSidebar` Team group (Sage W1) | Already redirected, orphan link is confusing |
48	
49	All three redirects in `next.config.ts` stay (preserve any deep links).
50	
51	### 3. P1 Fix — getAuthenticatedUser cookie-first
52	
53	S15 Sage review flagged: 134 API routes use `getAuthenticatedUser()` in `lib/supabase/server.ts:58-88`, which still reads `.order('created_at').limit(1).single()` against `studio_members`. The new StudioSwitcher writes a cookie, but the API layer ignores it → multi-studio users see data for studio A while the UI shows studio B.
54	
55	Fix: `getAuthenticatedUser()` reads `inkos_active_studio` cookie first, validates membership, falls back to first-membership. Single-point change, propagates to all 134 routes.
56	
57	### 4. Agency layer — **deferred to S17** (separate sprint)
58	
59	DB migration required (no `agency_id` / `organizations` table today). Concept:
60	- New `agencies` table: `id, name, slug, logo_url, owner_id, created_at`
61	- `studios.agency_id` FK, nullable
62	- Agency owner role for cross-studio dashboards (portfolio MRR, artist leaderboard, consolidated reports)
63	- `StudioSwitcher` extends to show an "Agency Portfolio" entry when `agencies.length >= 1`
64	
65	Reserved for S17 once a real agency customer is on the roadmap. Under-5% of target market for v1. S16 does not block this — cookie pattern is already in place.

1 # Vega Design Spec: Sprint S16 Part B — Persona Mode Switcher 2 3 **Project:** InkOS | **Stack:** A (Next.js 16 + Supabase + Railway) | **Date:** 2026-04-17 4 **Sprint:** S16 Part B of giggly-kindling-bee.md | **Depends on:** S15 (StudioSwitcher, LocationSwitcher, cookie pattern) 5 6 --- 7 8 ## Overview 9 10 `` is a segmented control that partitions the sidebar into three mental contexts: Operate / Manage / Configure. It lives inside `AppSidebar`, below the studio header block and above `SidebarContent`. Active mode is cookie-persisted server-side, resolved in layout. The component receives only resolved props — no internal cookie reads, no router inspection. 11 12 Roles with a single allowed mode receive `null` from the component (no DOM, no reserved space). Roles with two modes (receptionist) receive a 2-segment control. Roles with all three (admin, owner) receive the full 3-segment control. 13 14 --- 15 16 ## 1. Component Decision: Segmented Control 17 18 **Selection rationale:** 19 20 Segmented control wins over pill dropdown because: 21 - All allowed modes are always visible — no cognitive overhead of opening a menu to see what modes exist 22 - The component lives in the sidebar (not the header) so it has full sidebar width to work with — no horizontal space pressure 23 - Dropdown fits better when the choice list is dynamic and long (StudioSwitcher: N studios). Mode list is always 2–3 items and fixed. 24 - Collapsed sidebar degrades cleanly to an icon stack (visually identical to what shadcn's Sidebar already does with nav items) 25 26 Tabs (underline style) are rejected because they imply page-level section switching, not global app-context switching. The segmented control frame makes the "you are in a different mode" state more visually distinct. 27 28 --- 29 30 ## 2. Visual Specification 31 32 ### 2a. Expanded Sidebar Variant (`variant="expanded"`) 33 34 ``` 35 ┌──────────────────────────────────────────┐ 36 │ [container: rounded-lg bg-muted/40] │ 37 │ ┌──────────┬──────────┬──────────┐ │ 38 │ │ [active] │ │ │ │ 39 │ │ Operate │ Manage │ Configure│ │ 40 │ └──────────┴──────────┴──────────┘ │ 41 └──────────────────────────────────────────┘ 42 ``` 43 44 **Container (outer):** 45 ``` 46 className="flex rounded-[var(--radius)] bg-muted/40 p-[2px] gap-[2px]" 47 height: 32px total (h-8) 48 width: calc(100% − 16px) → achieved via mx-2 on the wrapper in AppSidebar 49 padding: p-[2px] (inner frame that contains segments) 50 ``` 51 52 **Segment button (each of 2 or 3):** 53 ``` 54 className="flex flex-1 items-center justify-center gap-1.5 rounded-[calc(var(--radius)-2px)] 55 h-7 px-2 text-[12px] font-medium leading-none 56 transition-all duration-100 focus-visible:outline-none focus-visible:ring-2 57 focus-visible:ring-ring focus-visible:ring-offset-1" 58 ``` 59 60 **Active segment:** 61 ``` 62 additional classes: "bg-background shadow-[var(--shadow-soft)] text-foreground font-semibold ring-1 ring-border/40" 63 ``` 64 65 The `bg-background` (pure white in light mode, ink-black-adjacent in dark) makes the active segment "float" off the muted container — same visual metaphor as the card/page bg relationship already in globals.css. 66 67 Do NOT use `bg-primary/10 text-primary` for the active state. content.text:
I see a significant concern. The `/api/context/set-mode` looks up role via `.limit(1).order('created_at')` — which matches the OLD first-membership pattern, NOT the currently active studio. This creates a bug and potential issue.

Let me think carefully:

- User has memberships in Studio A (role: admin) and Studio B (role: artist)
- First by created_at is Studio A (admin)
- They switch to Studio B via StudioSwitcher → cookie `inkos_active_studio=B`
- They should have artist role for mode resolution → allowed: `['operate']` only
- But `/api/context/set-mode` queries with `.limit(1).order('created_at')` → returns role `admin` from Studio A
- So user gets `getAllowedModes('admin')` = `['operate', 'manage', 'configure']`
- They can set mode=`manage` even though in active studio B they're just an artist

This is actually not a security escalation in terms of RLS (the mode cookie is purely nav filtering), but it IS a bug because:
1. The mode UI will show segments the user shouldn't see in Studio B
2. Since `getActiveMode()` in the layout uses the role from `getActiveStudio()` (which IS cookie-aware), it validates cookie against `getAllowedModes(Studio-B-role)` — so for artist in Studio B, even if mode cookie is 'manage', the resolution falls back to 'operate' anyway.

So the impact is:
- Server never honors invalid modes (defense in depth works in `getActiveMode`)
- The POST route accepts mode=`manage` when user's active studio role doesn't allow it (but since the layout validates on every read, the cookie is effectively dead)
- This is inconsistent with the proper pattern — the route should use the active studio's role
